system:
You are evaluating draft replies from an automated customer-support agent for Spotify's Twitter support account, as it operated in 2017.

Score the CANDIDATE REPLY on five criteria, each an integer 1-5.

correctness - Is what it says actually true for Spotify, and does it address what the customer asked?
  1 = wrong or answers a different question   3 = partially right, or vague but not wrong
  5 = accurate and on-point

groundedness - Is every claim supported by the PRECEDENTS shown?
  1 = main claims appear nowhere in the precedents   3 = loosely related to them
  5 = every factual claim traceable to a precedent

consistency - Does it handle this the way the precedents show Spotify handled similar cases (same action, same level of caution, same register)?
  1 = contradicts how Spotify handled these   3 = plausible but diverges
  5 = matches the precedents' approach

helpfulness - Does it move the customer forward?
  1 = useless or pure deflection   3 = generic but usable
  5 = a clear next step or a real answer

no_unsupported_claims - Does it avoid inventing policies, prices, timeframes, or promising account actions (refunds, resets, unlocks) the agent cannot perform?
  1 = makes a promise or states a policy with no support   3 = borderline hedged claim
  5 = makes no unsupported claim at all

Judge only the reply in front of you. The REFERENCE REPLY is what Spotify actually sent; it is context, not a target - a different but equally good reply should score well, and copying the reference does not automatically score 5.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"correctness": n, "groundedness": n, "consistency": n, "helpfulness": n, "no_unsupported_claims": n, "rationale": "<one sentence>"}

The Family Plan is a big rip off. I told you the day I signed up for it to cancel the family plan. Your foreign tech support was of no value. What I gathered from dialogue and their script only one of us can be on Spotify at a time. What a joke!!

PRECEDENTS:

[2066339] past customer: I'm thinking about getting Spotify next month do i get a free trial with the family plan
     spotify replied: 1: Hey Danny! We're afraid that trial offers are not valid for Premium for Family plans, but we have the free trial period for the...

[165043] past customer: me and my wife have separate spotify accounts but we want to get the family plan. Do one of us have cancel an account and get invited to the family plan? what about the payment plan? do the single accounts automatically switch to the family account?
     spotify replied: Hey Robert! Not to worry, you'll both be able to keep your accounts, all you'll have to decide is who will be the owner. For more information on the Family plan, check this out: <link> Hope this helps

[1147126] past customer: Hi I have the Spotify Family Plan. Is there any future plans to allow to invite more family members.
     spotify replied: Hey there! We don't have any info on this right now, but we'll let the right team know it's something you'd like to see 💚

[904729] past customer: I'm 28 days til the end of my AppleMusic trial. Spotify needs to get busy on an Apple Watch App or they lose a family customer
     spotify replied: Rest assured we'll also pass your feedback to the right folks! If you need anything else, just give us a shout

[1758260] past customer: If i buy spotify gift cards, does it work for the family plan?
     spotify replied: 1: Hey, help's here! We're afraid it won't work as you can't apply additional discounts to a Premium for Family plan.

CANDIDATE REPLY (score this):
hey there! we're afraid the info here doesn't address your concerns about cancellation or using Family at the same time. could you send us more details? 💚

REFERENCE REPLY actually sent by Spotify (context only):
Hey Hannah, help's here! With Premium for Family, you'll each keep your separate accounts with all of your own music. This means that your members can log in simultaneously. Also, can you DM us your account's email address? We'll look into it /GS <link>

Return the JSON scores.
